proposition: Letters 10 and 22 welcome the arrival of Fīrūzshāh's troops in Persian Iraq (ca. 817/1414 and ca. 827-28/1423-24); letter 22 calls it a boon to the scholars who had suffered from the region's unrest, and says Ibn Turka wishes to attend the amir's court at once but is prevented.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Amīr Fīrūzshāh
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
